match.reason: The bank point covers only how burning fossil fuels releases stored carbon, but the new point also needs the trade-offs of solar, wind and hydro power, which the bank point does not teach.

draft.title: Producing energy sustainably
card: Burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that adds to climate change.
Fossil fuels are also limited. They formed over millions of years, so the stores get smaller as they are used.
Solar, wind and hydro power (energy from moving water) release almost no carbon dioxide while they run. They draw on resources that are replaced.
These sources depend on weather and place. Solar panels need sunlight, wind turbines need wind, and hydro needs a river with enough flow.
draft.remember: Fossil fuels emit carbon dioxide and run down. Solar, wind and hydro emit less but depend on weather and place.

a.q: Why is burning coal for electricity a problem for the atmosphere?
opts: It releases carbon dioxide
It releases sunlight
It uses up the wind
It makes new coal stores
a.why: Burning coal releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas. Wind is not used up by burning coal, and coal does not form again in a human lifetime.
a.clue: Think about the gas released when fuel burns.

b.q: Priya wants to power her farm with a wind turbine, but her valley is often still and calm. What is the main problem with this plan?
opts: The turbine would make little power on calm days
The turbine would release a lot of carbon dioxide
The turbine would use up a limited fuel store
The turbine would need coal to start working
b.why: Wind power depends on weather, so calm days mean little power. The tempting answer about carbon dioxide is wrong, because wind turbines release almost none while running.
b.clue: Which of these depends on weather?

b.best: The turbine would make little power on calm days

problems.detail: The wrong options ('It releases sunlight', 'It uses up the wind', 'It makes new coal stores') are implausible for Years 7 and 8. A student can pick the answer without knowing the idea.
The clue 'Think about the gas released when fuel burns' gives the answer away, because only one option names a gas.

The clue 'Which of these depends on weather?' points straight at the only option about weather. The right option also echoes 'calm' from the question, so a student can match words without understanding.

card: Burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that adds to climate change.

These sources depend on weather and place. Solar panels need sunlight, wind turbines need wind, and hydro needs a river with enough flow.
proposal.remember: Fossil fuels emit carbon dioxide and run down. Solar, wind and hydro emit less but depend on weather and place.

a.q: Which statement about burning coal to make electricity is correct?
opts: It releases carbon dioxide and uses up a limited store
It releases carbon dioxide, but coal stores refill quickly
It releases only steam, but coal stores are limited
It releases only steam, and coal stores refill quickly
a.why: Burning coal releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas, and coal took millions of years to form, so its stores run down as it is used. The white clouds above some power stations are mostly steam, but the carbon dioxide is invisible, so 'only steam' is wrong.
a.clue: Check both halves of each option against the card.

b.q: Priya wants to power her farm with a wind turbine. Her valley has little wind for most of the year. What is the main problem with this plan?
opts: It would make little electricity for much of the year
It would release carbon dioxide as its blades turn
It would use up the wind in the valley over time
It would need coal burnt to keep its blades turning
b.why: Wind power depends on weather and place, so a valley with little wind gives little electricity. Wind is not used up, because it is a renewable resource that is replaced, and turbines release almost no carbon dioxide while they run.
b.clue: Test each option against how a wind turbine makes power.

a.best: It releases carbon dioxide and uses up a limited store

b.best: It would make little electricity for much of the year
